A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RLTHF research, with matching methods, datasets and experiments. Their text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original reward-model evaluations, downstream DPO results, hyperparameter studies and ablations on HH-RLHF and TL;DR.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and adds downstream HH-RLHF results using GPT-4o mini and a cost analysis.

M1.justification: The reward-based selection, preference flipping, human annotation, amplification, back-off, sharding and downstream transfer mechanisms are retained. Algorithm 1 documents the existing procedure; the revised amplification schedule is a reported experimental configuration change.

E1.justification: Both versions use HH-RLHF dialogue preferences and TL;DR summarization preferences. The added GPT-4o-mini configuration and cost case study use existing coverage, without introducing another dataset, task or input environment.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds GPT-4o-mini AI-labeled and corresponding Random baselines to the HH-RLHF downstream comparison, where v1 reported only GPT-4o-based variants. The broader comparator families and reward-model comparisons remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The default amplification changes from fixed alpha=4 in v1 Appendix C.4 to 4,4,4,2,1 across iterations, then 1, in v3 Appendix D.4. This establishes a reported setting revision, without establishing reruns. The added HH-RLHF/GPT-4o-mini downstream experiment specifies 7% human annotation; established metrics, models and evaluation prompts remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 4.3 and Appendix F add a cost case study testing whether annotation savings survive LLM-labeling and reward-model computation costs. Table 2 also extends downstream evidence for robustness to weaker initial labeling. Existing component ablations and sensitivity results in Figure 5 and Table 1 are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. The new 84.0–86.0% cost-saving range represents different model configurations, not statistical uncertainty.

E6.justification: Table 2 adds HH-RLHF/GPT-4o-mini win rates of 45.1% for AI-labeled, 46.3% for Random and 56.1% for RLTHF; existing table values remain unchanged. Section 4.1.1 now attributes 91.8%/89.6% accuracy to fully human-labeled training, replacing v1's wording about further improvements after full-dataset labeling. New cost tables report totals of $926.7/$813.3 versus $5788.8, yielding estimated savings of 84.0–86.0%.

T1.justification: The Bradley-Terry formulation, training loss, preference-orientation definitions, reward-difference property and assumptions are retained. The new pseudocode and cost arithmetic introduce no new theoretical result or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the central claims: targeted human feedback achieves full-human-level alignment using 6–7% annotation and produces downstream models outperforming fully human-annotated baselines. Revised wording and additional supporting evidence do not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: The new cost discussion explicitly weighs annotation savings against AI-labeling and iterative-training overhead. Appendix F argues that low assumed human-labeling prices make its savings estimate conservative. Existing explanations concerning sanitization, annotation efficiency and self-improvement limitations are largely retained.

D1.justification: Appendix B adds procedure pseudocode, and Appendix F supplies token counts, pricing assumptions, GPU memory and per-iteration timing estimates. The amplification configuration is revised explicitly. Most training hyperparameters, data preparation and evaluation templates were already documented in v1.

R1.justification: v3 adds Yu et al. (2025), RIP, to the self-improvement discussion and pricing/infrastructure references supporting the cost analysis. It removes Li et al. (2024), Learning from Contrastive Prompts. The overall positioning relative to RLHF, RLAIF and self-improvement remains stable.

P1.justification: v3 edits method explanations and rewrites portions of the experimental narrative while preserving the main section sequence. It inserts pseudocode and cost sections plus an Impact Statement; original appendices B–D become C–E. These are localized extensions and refinements rather than a wholesale restructuring.

P2.justification: Table 2 gains an HH-RLHF/GPT-4o-mini column, and v3 adds Algorithm 1 and cost Tables 4–5. Existing plots are retained with modest sizing, caption and placement changes. Publication headers and appendix layout also change.

improvement.justification: The pseudocode, additional HH-RLHF/GPT-4o-mini results and explicit computation-cost accounting improve clarity and evidential completeness. These are limited gains rather than a fundamental strengthening of the study. The cost analysis also has a mismatch: it assumes 6% human annotation for GPT-4o mini, whereas Section 4.2 uses 7%, limiting how directly its savings support the reported performance.
